title: This Lavender Tallow Balm Is Weird. My Skin Loves It.
body:
So I’m standing there, maybe 10:47 PM, and my face just feels… tight. You know that feeling. Like your skin decided to shrink two sizes. I’d just washed it with that cheap drugstore cleanser—the green one that always leaves me feeling sort of squeaky and sad. And I’m staring at this little jar I got in the mail. Whipped beef tallow balm. Lavender. Sounds like something you’d cook with, not smear on your face. My routine before this was a mess. A serum from a TikTok ad that made me break out, a moisturizer that sat on top of my skin like a plastic bag. I was skeptical, big time. But this tallow balm routine, this weird little lavender-scented fat from grass-fed cows in France, somehow became the only thing that made sense. Here’s how that happened.

## How I Started Putting Beef Fat on My Face

Look, it sounds gross. I get it. I thought the same thing. Tallow? For skin? But then I read something about how it’s similar to the oils our skin already makes. Sebum, or whatever. The logic was there, I guess. Mimics human skin stuff for better absorption. My hands were a disaster from all the hand sanitizer and spring wind—cracked, rough, just angry. My lips were perpetually chapped. I’d tried everything in a tube. Nothing worked for more than an hour. So I figured, why not. The worst that could happen is I smell like a herb-crusted roast. I ordered this whipped tallow balm from a small shop on Etsy, the Lavender one, because the description said “calming” and “sleep-promoting” and my anxiety brain was like, yes, please, inject calm directly into my face.

It arrived on a Tuesday. The jar was smaller than I pictured. I opened it right there in my kitchen, under the too-bright LED lights. The texture wasn’t what I expected. Not greasy. Not hard. It was… whipped. Like cool buttercream, but denser. I poked it. Weird. I scooped a tiny bit—the size of a pea, maybe less—and rubbed it between my fingers. It melted. Not into an oil slick, but into this… nothing. It just vanished into my skin. My fingers felt soft. Not slippery soft. Just normal, but better. No residue. That was the first surprise. I didn’t have to wipe my hands on my jeans. Huh.

## My Stupid Simple Tallow Balm Routine Now

Okay so my nightly thing. It’s not fancy. I wash my face. Sometimes I remember to use a warm cloth. Usually I don’t. My bathroom is cold in the spring evenings, the tile floor is awful, and the extractor fan hums like an angry bee. I grab the jar. I use my ring finger—I read that somewhere, less pressure—and get a dab. Smaller than a pea. Really, a tiny amount is all you need with this stuff, which is good because the jar isn’t huge. I rub it between my palms for a second to warm it up. Then I just… press it into my face. Forehead, cheeks, chin. I don’t rub it in hard. I just pat and press. It sounds dumb but it feels like a thing. A tiny ritual.

The lavender smell is there. It’s not a candle shop smell. It’s not “aromatherapy.” It’s just… lavender. Like the plant. Herbal. A little earthy. It doesn’t smell like dessert. It smells like the quiet part of a garden. It’s there when you put it on and then it’s gone in a minute. It doesn’t linger and mix with my pillow smell, which is good because my pillow probably smells like my hair product and regret. I put it on my lips too. Just a swipe. And then I always, always scoop the last bit off my fingers and rub it into the back of my hands. Those poor, cracked things.

That’s it. That’s the whole routine with this tallow balm. Some nights I’m in bed by 11:15. Some nights I’m scrolling on my phone until 1 AM, the blue light reflecting off the jar on my nightstand. But I do it almost every night. Because here’s the thing: when I wake up, my skin doesn’t feel tight. It doesn’t feel greasy. It just feels… like skin. Hydrated skin. Not “moisturized” in that fake, shiny way. Just normal. My lips aren’t stuck together in a dry, peeling mess. My hands look less like I’ve been digging in dirt. I don’t know how else to say it. It just works.

## What Actually Changed After a Few Weeks

I wasn’t tracking progress or anything. I’m not that person. But I noticed stuff. The fine lines around my eyes—the ones that look extra deep when I’m tired—seemed less… dramatic. Not gone. Just less angry-looking. The persistent dry patch I get on my left cheekbone every spring? Gone. Vanished. I didn’t even notice it leave. My partner, who never comments on this stuff, touched my face one morning and said, “Your skin is soft.” That was weird. And nice.

The biggest win was my hands, honestly. Daily skincare with tallow isn’t just for your face. After doing the hand thing every night for a couple weeks, the cracks healed. The roughness smoothed out. I didn’t have to constantly reapply lotion that would just wash off the second I touched water. I started keeping a tiny sample jar of it in my bag for my cuticles. It’s that versatile. I used it on a minor razor burn on my leg once. Worked better than the specialty cream I bought. It’s just… a good multi-tasking thing. A fix-it balm.

I got sidetracked looking at the Etsy shop again the other day. They have an unscented one too. I was thinking about getting it for my mom, whose hands get really bad in the dry weather. But then I remembered she hates the smell of lavender. Or maybe she doesn’t. I should call her.

## Would I Buy This Lavender Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did. I’m on my second jar. The first one lasted me a good three months, using it almost every day on my face, lips, and hands. That’s pretty good. It’s not cheap, but it’s not crazy expensive either, especially when you consider it replaced like three other products for me—night cream, lip balm, hand cream. I’m not a skincare guru. I don’t have a ten-step routine. I just have this one jar that does what it says it will do. It absorbs. It doesn’t clog my pores—and my skin is pretty finicky. It just… helps. It’s become a non-negotiable part of my night now. The little ritual of warming it up, the brief smell of lavender, the press-into-skin and done. It signals my brain that the day is over. Time to shut off.

It’s a weird product to explain to people. “Yeah, I use rendered beef fat on my face. From France.” It sounds pretentious and bizarre at the same time. But I don’t care. My skin is happy. I’m happy. That’s the whole point, right?

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Sounds wild, but yeah. The science-y reason is that it’s really similar to the oils our own skin produces. So it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top, and it doesn’t confuse your skin or clog pores like some synthetic stuff can. It just works with your skin, not against it.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not in my experience, and my pores are easily offended. Because it’s so similar to our skin’s sebum, it seems to absorb cleanly. It’s not a heavy, pore-clogging oil. It’s a balm that melts in. I was worried about this too, but it’s been totally fine.

**What does the lavender tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like actual lavender plants. Not a perfume, not a candle. It’s herbal and a little earthy—a timeless, clean herbal smell. It’s strong when you open the jar but fades really quickly once it’s on your skin. It’s calming without being overwhelming.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult, or dry, or just generally pissy, this might be worth a shot. I got mine from a little Etsy shop that makes them in small batches. I don’t know what else to say. It just works.
